findings.assertion: Rabell and Mier y Terán report that their survey of earthquake-displaced people staying in shelters and camps was designed six days after the first earthquake of September 1985, highlighting the unusually early collection of household evidence during the emergency.
findings.source_locator: 1986 Revista Mexicana de Sociología article HTML abstract, first sentence; pp.3–28 full text not read
findings.limitations: Survey design is reported in authors' abstract; sample sizes and full methodology not yet checked.

findings.assertion: A contemporary scholarly summary juxtaposes 3,745 damaged residential buildings in an emergency commission report, about 90,000 affected dwellings and 30,000 needing demolition in a CEPAL assessment, and government estimates of 46,000 families needing support, 25,000 directly affected. These refer to different units and assessments, not interchangeable estimates of one quantity.
findings.source_locator: Rabell and Mier y Terán 1986 HTML abstract, second-third sentences; González Salazar 1985 UNAM repository abstract (https://ru.iiec.unam.mx/1508/) provides contemporary preliminary comparison
findings.limitations: Original government/CEPAL reports, definitions and survey dates unexamined; numbers must remain author-attributed and cannot be used as single definitive damage total.

findings.assertion: Antonio Azuela de la Cueva states that the first of a series of reconstruction expropriation decrees appeared on 11 October 1985, involving several thousand central-city properties; his abstract describes an advantageous financing arrangement for beneficiaries emerging roughly six months later.
findings.source_locator: Azuela de la Cueva 1986 publisher HTML abstract paragraphs 1–2, pp.303–304 article not directly read
findings.limitations: Overlaps prior 1985 expropriation finding stg-20261112T195738Z-auto9-breadth-8ce5-f05; enrichment not independent corroboration. Original decree, precise lot list, financing instrument and beneficiary outcomes unexamined.

findings.assertion: An INAH retrospective catalog describes a historical-monument damage assessment commission established on 20 September 1985, the day after the first earthquake, to evaluate damage in the Centro Histórico; the associated text calls for thinking about conservation at the urban-unit scale.
findings.source_locator: INAH Antropología journal 2024 catalog/abstract: https://revistas.inah.gob.mx/index.php/antropologia/article/view/21642 ; contextual counterpart Morales 2019 catalog of a diagnosis presented 17 October 1985
findings.limitations: The INAH 2024 historical-monument damage assessment item is a separate metadata lead not yet registered as a standalone source here; original 1985 committee minutes and report not inspected. No specific building damage assigned.

findings.assertion: Leslie Serna interprets the Coordinadora Única de Damnificados as a movement active over approximately three years after 1985 whose negotiated proposals led to a Convenio de Concertación Democrática para la Reconstrucción defining reconstruction arrangements; her repository abstract credits the organization with broader citizenship and political effects.
findings.source_locator: UNAM institutional repository record 4146831, abstract and journal issue citation
findings.limitations: Author's retrospective interpretation from abstract only; agreement date, parties, legal form, and interview testimonies not inspected. Do not assert definitive causality or universal agreement.

findings.assertion: The UNAM description of Ziccardi, Mecatl and Michel's 1987 study says the reconstruction housing programs included an unusual objective of rebuilding replacement homes in earthquake-affected residents' original neighborhoods rather than relocating them elsewhere; this is a summary of the authors' findings, not a verified household-by-household outcome.
findings.source_locator: UNAM Instituto de Investigaciones Sociales digitized-book repository record IIS/5649 and catalog description via UNAM 1987 book record; full book unexamined
findings.limitations: No reconstruction address-level evidence or household interviews directly examined; no exact neighborhood success rates claimed.

findings.assertion: Ziccardi's 1986 study frames reconstruction as a problem of preexisting housing conditions in central delegations, the different circumstances of displaced residents, and the design of new housing policy, rather than purely post-earthquake engineering repair.
findings.source_locator: UNAM Instituto de Investigaciones Sociales IIS/5202 HTML catalog abstract, article pp.121–193 listed but full text not read
findings.limitations: Analytical scope of the published work, not direct proof of a particular government action; full article and local case studies need reading.
